newsitem.title: DUBAI: Saudi denies taking stand on foreign role in bomb.
newsitem.headline: Saudi denies taking stand on foreign role in bomb.

text.p: Saudi Arabia's interior minister said in remarks published on Wednesday he had neither confirmed nor denied a foreign power's role in the bombing of a military housing complex in Saudi Arabia which killed 19 U.S. airmen.
Recent U.S. media reports have alleged Saudi authorities had uncovered Iranian involvement in the June 25 bombing at the complex in Khobar, eastern Saudi Arabia.

But in an interview with the Saudi-owned Asharq al-Awsat daily on December 17, Interior Minister Prince Nayef described the reports as untrue and unreliable. He said Saudi Arabia was close to revealing the results of its investigations. "There

was nothing in my remarks published recently that confirms or denies any foreign power's role in this incident," he said in an interview with Wednesday's Riyadh daily, carried by state-run television. "Investigations are still under way. Details are
not clear yet," he was quoted as saying.
Prince Nayef made no mention of Iran or any other foreign state.
"We do not wish to jump to conclusions before the official results (of the investigations)," he was quoted as saying.
"The kingdom is very keen on confirming any information, whatever it may be, and to confirm the truth before making any announcements."

Saudi Arabia and its Gulf Arab allies often have tense relations with their non-Arab neighbour Iran. They have accused Tehran of interfering in their internal affairs and voiced concern over its arms build-up.

The Washington Post reported earlier this month that Saudi Arabia had given Washington detailed data to support the Saudis' alleged belief that the bombing was carried out by Shi'ite Moslems trained in Lebanon and backed by Iran.
The Los Angeles Times said Washington was making contingency plans for possible punitive action against Iran, including military strikes, if it was proven to be behind the attack.
Iran has denied the media reports.
